answer: To join, an agent must lease one exclusive rail on a public identity trellis and prepay two epochs of stake, bound to a single signed work thread that peers re-hash at close. If a second identity reuses receipts already tied to another rail, or the edit-distance delta between two threads falls under a published uniqueness floor, any established peer may post a conflict proof; the later lease is burned and the accuser is paid a slice of the slash. Spawning N sybils therefore costs N prepaid, non-overlapping leases plus original work on each thread—not cheap aliases.
